To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a transformer-based agent that uses two visual encoders -- one for scene classification and one for object detection -- can substantially improve the performance of VLN agents, and (2) this improvement is particularly large for navigation instructions that have a large number of object references, which suggests that our approach aligns visual object features more effectively to object references in the instructions

(1) a scene classification network provides a high-level context that helps to align object features to object references, (2) this alignment is learned by a vision-and-language pre-trained transformer that uses both the scene and object features, and (3) this approach improves performance on vision-and-language navigation benchmarks

(1) a transformer-based VLN agent with a scene encoder and an object detector is better than a transformer-based agent that uses an object detector only, (2) the agent with both encoders is better able to align object features and references in the instructions, and (3) our agent achieves the best reported performance on R2R.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of using scene and object features to support VLN.
how to best leverage visual cues in VLN, and how to best leverage vision-and-language pre-training for VLN.
the question of whether it is beneficial to use different visual representations for scene and object information.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our method is able to learn the alignment between images, objects, and language from pretraining data to substantially improve performance in vision-and-language navigation.
our approach is able to use object references in the instructions and align them to objects in the scene, which results in a better understanding of the navigation instructions.

our method is a transformer-based agent that uses two visual encoders to learn scene- and object-aware features for VLN, which leads to substantial improvements in performance on the R2R and RxR benchmarks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our method can better understand the visual world by using scene and object features, and this understanding can be transferred to downstream tasks like navigation.
our method is the first to use a scene-aware transformer for VLN and that it leads to state-of-the-art performance.
we propose a novel scene-and object-aware transformer (SOAT) that leverages scene and object information to improve the performance of VLN agents.
The main takeaway from our work is that
scene-level visual features can be useful for navigation instructions that include many object references.
a VLN agent can be designed to leverage different types of visual cues, and that such an agent can learn to align visual and language features from large-scale data.
a scene- and object-aware transformer can improve VLN performance by leveraging pretraining on vision-and-language data and by using a multi-modal architecture that is tailored to the task.
